newsitem.title: JAPAN: Greenspan supports BOJ law revision - BOJ official.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan supports BOJ law revision - BOJ official.

text.p: U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan told Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita on Monday that he supports revision of the BOJ law in a way that would strengthen the independence of the Japanese central bank, a BOJ official told reporters.

Greenspan and Matsushita met earlier today, and also discussed the monetary and economic situations of their countries and the rest of the world, the BOJ official said. He said he could not disclose the content of their discussion.
"Greenspan said he supports a revision of the BOJ law aimed at strengthening the BOJ's independence," the official said.
He added that Greenspan and Matsushita spent most of their meeting discussing the revision of the BOJ law.
Matsushita explained the proposals for the revision of the BOJ law, which a study group under the prime minister unveiled last week.
The official said Greenspan and Matsushita talked about Japan's planned financial reforms, but declined to disclose what they said.
Proposals for the reform of Japan's financial system were unveiled last week by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
Greenspan arrived in Japan on Sunday, and is scheduled to stay until Tuesday.
